_comment: Per-environment flash budget, in bytes, checked by tools/check_flash_budget.py.
The number compared is the one PlatformIO itself prints ('Flash: ... used N
bytes from M bytes'), not a size computed here — a gate that reimplements the
measurement is a gate that can disagree with what the developer sees.
A budget is a HIGH-WATER MARK, not the linker ceiling. The linker already
refuses an image that does not fit; what it cannot do is make growth visible
while there is still room. Each budget sits a few KB above the measured size
at the time it was set, so ordinary work passes and a jump has to be paid for
by editing this file in the same change — which puts the number in the diff,
where a reviewer sees it.
Raising a budget is a normal thing to do. Raising it without saying why in the
commit message is not.
'headroom' is documentation, not enforcement: measured - budget is what the
gate allows; ceiling - measured is what the hardware allows. Note the ceiling
reported by PlatformIO is the program slot alone and says nothing about the
LittleFS partition behind it (see docs/ANALISE_FLASH_RAM.md).
2026-09-09: 'used' is the SUM OF SECTIONS and understates the footprint. The
linker aligns .data's load address to 4 KiB, so the .bin (what the slot
actually holds) is larger by the padding: pico_w_air 1,025,600 used vs a
1,039,508 B .bin, 4,972 B of real slack. Real slack moves in 4 KiB steps -
readelf -l firmware.elf, end of the last LOAD in flash, is the number.
2026-09-11 (feat/fleet-api): the OTA-safe ceiling is 1,040,384 B of .bin (1016 KiB,
OTA_APP_SAFE_MAX_SIZE), not the 1,044,480 program slot: the last 4 KiB sector of
the slot is where the config snapshot lands at stage time. pico_w_air's .bin is
1,039,508 B on main AND on this branch - 876 B of real OTA slack, not 4,972.
The Air budget margin is 1,000 B for that reason; every future byte there is a trade.
2026-09-18 (feat/screen-mirror): the three TFT budgets go up because the panel
mirror landed - /api/screen_stream, its palette-RLE codec, POST /api/touch and the
dashboard canvas that drives them. release 1,024,340 -> 1,027,852, test +3,408,
asserts +3,528; the margin stays the 3,000 B this file has always used. alpha and
air keep their old budgets: neither has a panel, so both carry only the ~1.5 kB of
gzipped page, and both still fit.
2026-09-19 (study/core1-pause-mirror): 'measured' moves up and the budgets do
NOT. The panel mirror's Core-1 pause became a park without the SDK lockout, and
Core 1 idles for the length of a capture: +816 B on release, +968 on test,
+56 on alpha and +8 on air - the two imageless builds carry only the microsecond
stamps. Every environment is still inside the 3,000 B margin this file has
always used, so nothing here had to be raised; what would have been dishonest is
leaving 'measured' describing an image that no longer exists.
2026-09-19 (second pass): the budgets for the four panel builds GO UP, and this
is the raise the rule asks to be argued for. The mirror gained a DMA read
pipeline, a send-coalescing buffer and a second wire codec: +2,048 B on release,
and the 3,000 B margin this file has always carried had fallen to 136 B - on
pico_w_test it went 32 B negative, which is the gate doing its job. Budgets are
reset to measured + 3,000 so the next ordinary change is not blocked by a margin
that quietly ran out. alpha and air move by 16 and 8 B (a constexpr and a header
they barely touch) and keep their own margins, 2,928 and 1,000.
2026-09-19 (feat/alarms-live-config): +2,896 B on release, +6,352 on alpha,
+2,208 on air. Three things: a per-slot maintenance window (CONFIG_VERSION 23,
tail-append), a third payload domain in the alarm line, and ConfigApply.h -
which classifies what a commit changed so the handler reboots only for what
needs it. ConfigApply started as thirty hand-written compare/copy functions and
cost 4,488 B; rewritten as one span table walked by one loop it costs 2,896 and
the two halves can no longer drift apart. Budgets go to measured + 3,000 (air
keeps its 1,000); the air .bin is 1,027,116 B, 13,268 under the OTA ceiling.
2026-09-19 (feat/alarms-live-config, identity at the panel):
+15,792 B on release, +16,912 test, +16,936 test_https,
+15,800 asserts, +1,728 alpha, +6,848 air. CONFIG_VERSION 24: 32
accounts (five until v23), a per-account panel PIN (HMAC-SHA256 chain, 200 rounds,
device-wide salt, looked up BY the PIN), per-sensor alarm actions behind three new
permission bits, a Users item on the panel, five payload codes that carry the acting
user, twelve log codes. The screens (DisplayManager_Users.cpp) and their Core-0 side
(AppManager_Panel.cpp) are TFT-only: the first cut of AppManager_Panel.cpp compiled
into every environment and cost the Air 10,304 B; behind SIMUT_DISPLAY_TFT it costs
6,848 - the migration, the PIN hashing, the CLI and web PIN paths and the wider
account table, all of which every build carries. 72 B of the release delta are the
two follow-ups the rig asked for: Core 1 consuming _repaintSettings before a draw
instead of after it (a Core-0 screen change during a draw was lost, 7 of 7 logins),
and the sensor menu opening on the first row the account may use. Budgets go to
measured + 3,000 (air keeps 1,000); the air .bin is 1,031,212 B, 9,172 under the
OTA ceiling, the release .bin 1,008,300 B, 32,084 under it.
